record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Let L be a regular triangular lattice in the plane. Let f (z) map D onto the universal covering surface over the complement of L. Is it true that the coefficients an of f tend to 0 as n → ∞? (Ch. Pommerenke)

evidence.quote: Let L be a regular triangular lattice in the plane. Let f (z) map D onto the universal covering surface over the complement of L. Is it true that the coefficients an of f tend to 0 as n → ∞? (Ch. Pommerenke)
See Update 5.7. An affirmative answer was given by Hayman, Pommerenke and Patterson [416]. They proved that an = O (log n)−1/2 in this case.

artifact.category_tag: universal covering maps and Taylor coefficients
artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc. Let $L\subset\mathbb{C}$ be a regular triangular lattice, that is, the set of vertices of a tiling of the plane by congruent equilateral triangles. Let $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}\setminus L$ be a holomorphic universal covering map of the complement of $L$, and write its Taylor expansion at the origin as $f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_n z^n$. Determine whether $a_n\to 0$ as $n\to\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was answered affirmatively by Hayman, Pommerenke, and Patterson, who established the stronger bound $a_n = O((\log n)^{-1/2})$ for the universal covering map of the complement of a regular triangular lattice.

status_evidence.claim: The problem has been solved affirmatively with quantitative bound.
